sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- search: Search the web via the local SearXNG instance (titles, URLs, snippets)
- fetch: Fetch a specific http/https URL directly and return its text content (HTML → plain text)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use search to look up current web information or documentation.
- Use search with max_results when fewer or more results are needed (max 10).
- Use search with freshness to look only for recent results (day, week, month, year), category to restrict the result type (e.g. it, news, images), language to pin the result language (e.g. de, en), and page (1–10) to paginate beyond the first result page.
- If a filtered search returns no results, retry with fewer filters: on this container, freshness only applies to a small set of engines per category (e.g. 'it' covers only hackernews, 'news' just two), so 0 results can mean that engine set simply had no hits — broaden the category or drop freshness.
- Use fetch to read the text content of a specific page URL.
- Use fetch with max_chars to limit output length for long pages (hard cap 20000).
- Use fetch with offset to continue reading a long page (the next offset is given in the truncation notice), and raw=true to get the unmodified body without HTML→text conversion (e.g. JSON APIs).
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.project_context:
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/julian/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# Global instructions
As soon as your task is to programm something allways prioritize Test Driven Development (TDD) than do so.
Prefer simple, robust and performant solutions and check if something can get broken before making changes. Make sure to test against breaking changes.
Allways start your answer with a short abstract of what you want to say. After that you can write down your full response.
The last part every answer has to include is instructions for the user and what he has to do next. If there is nothing to do also tell the user.
Allways stick to english as our primary communication language.
Whenever you think you read something interesting about the user you can persist this knowledge into `~/.pi/agent/USER.md` so you can evolve into an even better assistant.

<!-- pi-env:start (managed by setup-pi-tools.sh) -->
## Safety rules (all projects)
- Git: use only read-only git commands (status, diff, log, show, ls-files, rev-parse, blame). Never run `git init` or any other git command that changes or creates a repository, unless I ask for that exact command in my own message. A "yes" to another question is not such a request.
- Never delete directories recursively (`rm -r`, `rm -rf`) and never overwrite files outside the scope of the current task without asking me first.
- If a command is blocked by the confirmation-dialog extension or declined by me, do not retry it in another form (no `sh -c`, aliases, scripts, or full paths). Continue without it, or ask me to run it myself.
- Never create `.pi/` files or scan the whole directory when running directly in my home directory; ask which project directory is meant.

## Planning and memory
- When a task should be planned before it is executed (new feature, workflow change, larger bug), use the `plan` skill.
- If the project has `.pi/LOG.md`: after a compaction or at the start of a session, read `.pi/PLAN.md` and `tail -n 60 .pi/LOG.md` before doing anything else.

## CLI tools (call them via bash)
- `rg` (ripgrep): search code and text. Use `-n`, single-quoted patterns, `-M 200`; `-l` for file names only, `-F` for literal text, `-w` for whole words, `-U` for patterns spanning several lines. `rg --files -g '*name*'` finds files by name.
- `ctags -x --sort=no <file>`: outline of a file (functions, classes, methods with line numbers). Always use `-x`; without it ctags writes a `tags` file.
- `jq '<filter>' <file.json>`: query JSON (e.g. `jq '.scripts' package.json`) instead of reading the whole file.
- Read files with `read` and `offset`/`limit` instead of `cat`; check the length with `wc -l` first. Keep command output small (`| head -50`).
<!-- pi-env:end -->

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: search
toolsAdded.description: Durchsucht das Web über die lokale SearXNG-Instanz nach aktuellen Informationen und Dokumentationen. Liefert die Top-Ergebnisse mit Titel, URL und Snippet.

freshness.description: Zeitfenster der Ergebnisse (optional): day | week | month | year

toolsAdded.name: fetch
toolsAdded.description: Lädt den Textinhalt einer spezifischen http/https-URL direkt herunter (HTML wird lokal in Plain-Text umgewandelt). Lange Seiten werden auf max_chars Zeichen gekürzt und können per offset in Stücken gelesen werden. Mit raw=true wird der Körper unverändert zurückgegeben (z. B. für JSON-APIs).

offset.description: Startposition in Zeichen zum Lesen langer Seiten in Stücken (default 0). Wenn die Seite gekürzt wird, erneut aufrufen mit offset=<returned_end> (steht in der Kürzungsnotiz).

raw.description: true: Körper unverändert zurückgeben (keine HTML→Text-Umwandlung, keine Content-Type-Prüfung); max_chars und offset gelten trotzdem. Für JSON-APIs nützlich.

Backup task (safety-critical, verify before deleting anything):

   SOURCE: /run/media/julian/DB3C-BF68  (14.5 GiB USB stick)
   TARGET: /run/media/julian/1TB_JULIAN  (1 TB disk, ~500 GB free)
                                                                                                                                                                            ·
   Goal: ensure every file on the stick exists on the 1 TB disk, then delete the                                                                                            ·
   verified files from the stick.                                                                                                                                           ·
                                                                                                                                                                            ▸
   Protocol (follow exactly, no shortcuts):
   1. Use absolute paths in every command. Never rely on the working directory.
   2. Enumerate all files on the stick: find + sizes. Check filenames contain no
      tabs/newlines; check NUL-count == line-count.
   3. Identify where this stick's data belongs on the disk. Previous stick's data
      (Bausatz VPS Aufgaben, Gefangenen Assets, Julian Franz, Praxis Übungen,
      Schlosser, Theorie - Infos+Unterrichtsmaterial, VDE-Bestimmungen) was backed
      up under "/run/media/julian/1TB_JULIAN/Backup Anstalt/Schulserver/". If the
      new stick's top-level folders match that pattern, use that mapping;
      otherwise search the 1 TB disk for matching relative paths and show me the
      mapping before proceeding.
   4. Match EVERY file one by one by name + size (join/comm, LC_ALL=C).
      Classify: SAME (name+size match) / SIZE_MISMATCH / MISSING.
      Report counts. If any SIZE_MISMATCH: do NOT delete those files, show the
      list and stop to ask me.
   5. Aggregate check: sum of all matched file sizes on stick == sum on disk.
   6. Content spot-check: SHA-256 compare a sample (~100 random + 10 largest +
      10 smallest). Any mismatch => stop and report.
   7. Copy only MISSING files into the mapped location (preserve paths).
      Verify each copied file by size + SHA-256 before it counts as backed up.
   8. Only after everything is verified: delete from the stick exactly the listed
      verified paths (xargs -d '\n' rm -- < list, no wildcards, no -r).
      Deleting ~18k small files on USB takes ~10-15 min and may exceed your
      command timeout: run it in the background (setsid nohup ... &) and poll
      the remaining file count until done; resume from a fresh "remaining" list
      if a timeout interrupts it (all remaining files are still verified).
   9. Skip "System Volume Information" (Windows metadata) by default; mention it
      in the final report. Do not remove empty directories without my approval.
   10. Final report: counts matched/copied/deleted, bytes totals, remaining
       files on stick, disk file count before/after (must only grow by the
       number of copied files).

   Authorization: files verified to exist on the 1 TB disk (name+size+checksum
   per protocol) are pre-approved for deletion from the stick. Nothing else may
   be deleted or modified. Never use rm -r / rm -rf.

  nmiss=$(wc -l < $W/${tag}_missing.tsv)

#!/bin/bash
# Step 7: copy only the MISSING files, verify each by size + SHA-256.
set -u
export LC_ALL=C
W=/tmp/backup_task
STICK=/run/media/julian/DB3C-BF68
DISK='/run/media/julian/1TB_JULIAN/Backup Anstalt/Schulserver'

declare -A SROOT=( [austausch]="$STICK/Austausch Schulnetzwerk"
                   [meinlaufwerk]="$STICK/Schulnetzwerk mein Laufwerk"
                   [lf5]="$STICK/LF 5 (Julian) Schutzmaßnahmen & Energieversorgung" )
declare -A DROOT=( [austausch]="$DISK/Austausch Schulnetzwerk"
                   [meinlaufwerk]="$DISK/Schulnetzwerk mein Laufwerk"
                   [lf5]="$DISK/Theorie - Infos+Unterrichtsmaterial/LF 5 (Julian) Schutzmaßnahmen & Energieversorgung" )

: > $W/copied_verified.txt
: > $W/copy_failures.txt
n=0
total=$(wc -l < $W/austausch_missing.tsv)
total=$((total + $(wc -l < $W/meinlaufwerk_missing.tsv) + $(wc -l < $W/lf5_missing.tsv)))

for tag in austausch meinlaufwerk lf5; do
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r rel size; do
    n=$((n+1))
    sp="${SROOT[$tag]}/$rel"
    dp="${DROOT[$tag]}/$rel"
    if [ -e "$dp" ]; then
      echo "ABORT-UNEXPECTED: destination already exists: $dp" | tee -a $W/copy_failures.txt
      continue
    fi
    mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "$dp")"
    if ! cp -p -- "$sp" "$dp"; then
      echo "COPY-FAIL $tag $rel" >> $W/copy_failures.txt
      continue
    fi
    # verify size
    dsize=$(stat -c %s -- "$dp")
    ssize=$(stat -c %s -- "$sp")
    # verify sha256
    hs=$(sha256sum -- "$sp" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    hd=$(sha256sum -- "$dp" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    if [ "$dsize" = "$size" ] && [ "$ssize" = "$size" ] && [ "$hs" = "$hd" ]; then
      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$tag" "$rel" "$size" >> $W/copied_verified.txt
    else
      echo "VERIFY-FAIL $tag $rel (stick=$ssize disk=$dsize expected=$size h_s=${hs:0:12} h_d=${hd:0:12})" >> $W/copy_failures.txt
    fi
    [ $((n % 25)) -eq 0 ] && echo "progress: $n/$total" >&2
  done < $W/${tag}_missing.tsv
done

echo
echo "processed: $n/$total"
echo "verified copies: $(wc -l < $W/copied_verified.txt)"
echo "verified bytes:  $(awk -F'\t' '{s+=$3} END {print s+0}' $W/copied_verified.txt)"
echo "failures:        $(wc -l < $W/copy_failures.txt)"
[ -s $W/copy_failures.txt ] && { echo '=== FAILURES ==='; cat $W/copy_failures.txt; exit 1; }
echo "STEP 7 OK: all copied files verified"
